title: अध्याय ३८

items.text: अष्टत्रिंशोऽध्यायः
items.tr: aṣṭatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ

items.speaker: जड उवाच
items.text:
दत्तात्रेयं ततो विप्रं प्रणिपत्य स पार्थिवः ।
प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं प्रश्रयावनतो वचः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
dattātreyaṃ tato vipraṃ praṇipatya sa pārthivaḥ |
pratyuvāca mahātmānaṃ praśrayāvanato vacaḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
सम्यक् प्रपश्यतो ब्रह्मन् ! मम दुः खं न किञ्चन ।
असम्यग्दर्शिना मग्नाः सर्वदैवासुखार्णवे ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
samyak prapaśyato brahman ! mama duḥ khaṃ na kiñcana |
asamyagdarśinā magnāḥ sarvadaivāsukhārṇave || 2 ||

items.text:
यस्मिन् यस्मिन्ममासक्ता बुद्धिः पुंसः प्रजायते ।
ततस्ततः समादाय दुः खान्येव प्रयच्छति ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
yasmin yasminmamāsaktā buddhiḥ puṃsaḥ prajāyate |
tatastataḥ samādāya duḥ khānyeva prayacchati || 3 ||

items.text:
मार्जारभक्षिते दुः खं यादृशं गृहकुक्कुटे ।
न तादृङ्ममताशून्ये कलविङ्केऽथ मूषिके ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
mārjārabhakṣite duḥ khaṃ yādṛśaṃ gṛhakukkuṭe |
na tādṛṅmamatāśūnye kalaviṅke'tha mūṣike || 4 ||

items.text:
सोऽहं न दुः खी न सुखी यतोऽहं प्रकृतेः परः ।
यो भूताभिभवो भूतैः सुखदुः खात्मको हि सः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
so'haṃ na duḥ khī na sukhī yato'haṃ prakṛteḥ paraḥ |
yo bhūtābhibhavo bhūtaiḥ sukhaduḥ khātmako hi saḥ || 5 ||

items.speaker: दत्तात्रेय उवाच
items.text:
एवमेतन्नरव्याघ्र ! यथैतद्व्याहृतं त्वया ।
ममेति मूलं दुः कस्य न ममेति च निर्वृतेः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
evametannaravyāghra ! yathaitadvyāhṛtaṃ tvayā |
mameti mūlaṃ duḥ kasya na mameti ca nirvṛteḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
मत्प्रश्नादेव ते ज्ञानमुत्पन्नमिदमुत्तमम् ।
ममेति प्रत्ययो येन क्षिप्तः शाल्मलितूलवत् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
matpraśnādeva te jñānamutpannamidamuttamam |
mameti pratyayo yena kṣiptaḥ śālmalitūlavat || 7 ||

items.text:
अहमित्यङ्कुरोत्पन्नो ममेति स्कन्धवान् महान् ।
गृहक्षेत्रोच्चशाखश्च पुत्रदारादिपल्लवः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
ahamityaṅkurotpanno mameti skandhavān mahān |
gṛhakṣetroccaśākhaśca putradārādipallavaḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
धनधान्यमहापत्रो नैककालप्रवर्धितः ।
पुण्यापुण्याग्रपुष्पश्च सुखदुः खमहाफलः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
dhanadhānyamahāpatro naikakālapravardhitaḥ |
puṇyāpuṇyāgrapuṣpaśca sukhaduḥ khamahāphalaḥ || 9 ||

items.text:
तत्र मुक्तिपथव्यापि मूढसम्पर्कसेचनः ।
विधित्साभृङ्गमालाढ्यो कृत्यज्ञानमहातरुः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tatra muktipathavyāpi mūḍhasamparkasecanaḥ |
vidhitsābhṛṅgamālāḍhyo kṛtyajñānamahātaruḥ || 10 ||

items.text:
संसाराध्वपरिश्रान्ता ये तच्छायां समाश्रिताः ।
भ्रान्तिज्ञानसुखाधीनास्तेषामात्यन्तिकं कुतः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
saṃsārādhvapariśrāntā ye tacchāyāṃ samāśritāḥ |
bhrāntijñānasukhādhīnāsteṣāmātyantikaṃ kutaḥ || 11 ||

items.text:
यैस्तु सत्सङ्गपाषाणशितेन ममतातरुः ।
छिन्नो विद्याकुठारेण ते गतास्तेन वर्त्मना ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
yaistu satsaṅgapāṣāṇaśitena mamatātaruḥ |
chinno vidyākuṭhāreṇa te gatāstena vartmanā || 12 ||

items.text:
प्राप्य ब्रह्मवनं शीतं नीरजस्कमकण्टकम् ।
प्राप्नुवन्ति परां प्राज्ञा निर्वृतिं वृत्तिवर्जिताः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
prāpya brahmavanaṃ śītaṃ nīrajaskamakaṇṭakam |
prāpnuvanti parāṃ prājñā nirvṛtiṃ vṛttivarjitāḥ || 13 ||

items.text:
भूतेन्द्रियमयं स्थूलं न त्वं राजन्न चाप्यहम् ।
न तन्मात्रमयावावां नैवान्तः करणात्मकौ ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
bhūtendriyamayaṃ sthūlaṃ na tvaṃ rājanna cāpyaham |
na tanmātramayāvāvāṃ naivāntaḥ karaṇātmakau || 14 ||

items.text:
कं वा पश्यामि राजेन्द्र ! प्रधानमिदमावयोः ।
यतः परो हि क्षेत्रज्ञः सङ्घातो हि गुणात्मकः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
kaṃ vā paśyāmi rājendra ! pradhānamidamāvayoḥ |
yataḥ paro hi kṣetrajñaḥ saṅghāto hi guṇātmakaḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
मशकोडुम्बरेषीकामुञ्जमत्स्याम्भसां यथा ।
एकत्वेऽपि पृथग्भावस्तथा क्षेत्रात्मनोर्नृप ! ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
maśakoḍumbareṣīkāmuñjamatsyāmbhasāṃ yathā |
ekatve'pi pṛthagbhāvastathā kṣetrātmanornṛpa ! || 16 ||

items.speaker: अलर्क उवाच
items.text:
भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन ममाविर्भूतमुत्तमम् ।
ज्ञानं प्रधानचिच्छक्ति-विवेककरमीदृशम् ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
bhagavaṃstvatprasādena mamāvirbhūtamuttamam |
jñānaṃ pradhānacicchakti-vivekakaramīdṛśam || 17 ||

items.text:
किन्त्वत्र विषयाक्रान्ते स्थैर्यवत्त्वं न चेतसि ।
न चापि वेद्मि मुच्येयं कथं प्रकृतिबन्धनात् ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
kintvatra viṣayākrānte sthairyavattvaṃ na cetasi |
na cāpi vedmi mucyeyaṃ kathaṃ prakṛtibandhanāt || 18 ||

items.text:
कथं न भूयां भूयश्च कथं निर्गुणतामियाम् ।
कथञ्च ब्रह्मणैकत्वं व्रजेयं शाश्वतेन वै ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
kathaṃ na bhūyāṃ bhūyaśca kathaṃ nirguṇatāmiyām |
kathañca brahmaṇaikatvaṃ vrajeyaṃ śāśvatena vai || 19 ||

items.text:
तन्मे योगन्तथा ब्रह्मन् ! प्रणतायाभियाचते ।
सम्यग् ब्रूहि महाप्राज्ञ ! सत्सङ्गो ह्युपकृन्नृणाम् ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
tanme yogantathā brahman ! praṇatāyābhiyācate |
samyag brūhi mahāprājña ! satsaṅgo hyupakṛnnṛṇām || 20 ||

en_summary: Alarka bows to Dattatreya and says that, seeing rightly, he has no sorrow; those who see wrongly are always sunk in an ocean of unhappiness. Whatever a person's mind becomes attached to as 'mine' brings him only sorrow: the grief when a cat eats one's own hen is not felt when it eats a sparrow or mouse that one does not own. He is neither sad nor happy, since he is beyond Nature (Prakriti); pleasure and pain belong to the elements acting on elements. Dattatreya agrees: 'mine' is the root of sorrow and 'not mine' the root of peace; by his questioning this knowledge has arisen in Alarka and thrown off the idea of 'mine' like silk-cotton fluff. He describes a great tree of wrong knowledge: it sprouts from 'I', its trunk is 'mine', house and land are its high branches, sons and wife its shoots, wealth and grain its great leaves, merit and sin its flowers, joy and sorrow its fruit; it blocks the path to freedom, is watered by the company of fools, and is full of the bees of craving; those tired by the road of worldly life who rest in its shade, depending on the pleasure of false knowledge, never find lasting good. But those who cut down this tree of 'mine' with the axe of knowledge, sharpened on the stone of good company, go by the path to the cool forest of Brahman, free of dust and thorns, and gain supreme peace. Neither Alarka nor he is the gross body of elements and senses, nor the subtle elements, nor the inner organ; the knower of the field (the Self) is beyond, and the aggregate is made of the qualities; as a gnat and the udumbara fruit, a reed and its sheath, a fish and water are together yet separate, so are the field and the Self. Alarka says that by his grace he now knows the difference between Nature and the power of consciousness, but his mind, held by sense objects, is not steady, and he does not know how to be freed from the bondage of Nature, how not to be born again, how to go beyond the qualities and become one with the eternal Brahman. He asks Dattatreya to teach him yoga, since the company of the good helps people.
